curated.instructions: omr/instructions/852-1/ (scans; the helicopter is pages 1-10, the plane after is an alternate)

functions.does: The handwheel on the cabin's right side turns both rotors: through a crown gear and an 8-tooth gear it drives the 24-tooth gear on the upright rotor mast, slowly, and through a lengthwise shaft with universal joints running back along the tail boom it turns the tail rotor, faster.

The two control sticks in front of the seats, on one cross shaft, raise and lower the collar on the rotor mast: two bellcranks under the floor push two rods up behind the seats, and short links from the collar's spinning half twist both rotor blades, changing their pitch together.
functions.source: book: steps 2-5 (the rod frame), 9-10 and 16-17 (the rotor head); inferred: no motion is drawn, and unsure that the sticks are meant to work the blade pitch rather than tilt the rotor

functions.does: The landing skids stand fixed under the cabin on four struts, braced by two cross axles and two rods between them.
functions.source: book: step 20 and its inset; inferred: that the frame is meant to be rigid
functions.note: KineBrick today lets the whole skid frame swing fore and aft on its struts (dragging p308 swings both skids).

questions.question: Do the sticks change the blades' pitch together, or tilt the rotor? Should the skids be rigid?
